meta.title: Replace Math.DivRem with bit operations in BitArray for WASM performance
meta.body_summary: Replace Math.DivRem with bitwise shifts and masks in BitArray to mitigate 1.1x-5.4x WASM performance regressions caused by inefficient WASM code generation for constant divisions.

perf_labels.notes: Copilot replaced Math.DivRem with bit ops; maintainers rejected library-level workaround, insisting proper fix is JIT intrinsic for constant division; PR reverted and auto-closed after inactivity.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: A tiny change (56 lines, one file) that would have been a small-step performance improvement, but it was closed because the approach was architecturally incorrect—the optimization belongs in the WASM JIT backend, not in the managed library.

review_details.concern_detail: Maintainers (EgorBo, tannergooding) argued that Math.DivRem with constant divisor should be optimized by the WASM backend (or even generic JIT), not by manually replacing it with bit operations in the library; this is a broader compiler issue.
review_details.performance_claim: Eliminate 1.1x-5.4x WASM slowdowns in BitArray operations by replacing Math.DivRem with bitwise shifts and masks.
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainers unanimously agreed the fix should be in the JIT, not the library; PR reverted and later auto-closed as draft after 30 days of inactivity.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Copilot attempted a library-level workaround that was architecturally inferior to the correct fix (JIT intrinsic for constant division). It lacked the understanding of where optimization should be applied in a layered runtime.

detection_detail.code_reading: EgorBo and tannergooding reviewed the BitArray change and recognized it as a symptom of missing JIT optimization rather than a library issue.
detection_detail.ci_auto: lewing referenced a CoreCLR perf autofiling issue (#58144) showing the regression is not WASM‑only, validating that the problem lies in code generation.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No before/after benchmark data or profiler output was provided in the PR; only narrative claims about micro‑benchmark results.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After maintainer feedback, Copilot reverted all changes in commit f40fc8c. The PR then remained inactive and was automatically closed by a policy bot after 30 days.

core_change_summary.description: In BitArray.cs, replaced Math.DivRem with bitwise shifts (>>3 for /8, >>5 for /32) and masks (&7 for %8, &31 for %32) across methods Get, Set, ClearHighExtraBits, CopyTo, RightShift, and LeftShift.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: replaced Math.DivRem calls with bit operations.
After maintainer feedback, a revert commit restored all original Math.DivRem calls.

review_signals.summary: This should be done inside the WASM backend; not something to pollute the codebase with.
Agreed the correct fix is to update the WASM backend to recognize Math.DivRem as intrinsic and optimize it.
Pointed out the regression also affects CoreCLR, indicating a broader JIT issue.
Draft Pull Request was automatically closed for 30 days of inactivity.

collaboration_trajectory: Copilot opened draft PR with bit-operation replacement.
EgorBo commented within hours that the fix belongs in WASM backend, not library.
Copilot engaged in discussion, eventually reverting all changes after tannergooding and others concurred.
Discussion continued for a day about the actual JIT issue and possible AMD‑only scope; no further commits were made.
PR remained open as draft, then was auto‑closed by dotnet‑policy‑service after 30 days of inactivity.
